newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken not factored into Sweden debt - official.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken not factored into Sweden debt - official.

text.p: Sweden's National Debt Office said on Thursday the money the state would receive from the proposed share buy back by Nordbanken had not yet been factored into the state's projected borrowing needs for 1996.
The office's most recent forecast for the state borrowing need for the year, released on Tuesday, was 40 and 50 billion crowns for 1996.

"The effect of the buy back would be that the state would receive five billion crowns to reduce its borrowing requirement by a comparable amount," National Debt Office spokeswoman Anette Persson told Reuters.
The Swedish state said it would receive at most five billion crowns and at least 3.275 billion crowns from the proposed five billion crown buy back by state-controlled bank Nordbanken.
Nordbanken on Wednesday announced a share buy back that could reduce the government's holding to 58 percent from 65.5 percent of the bank that it bailed out in 1992 after a loan-loss crisis.

Swedish daily newspaper Dagens Industri said gains in the state coffers would help Sweden reduce the state debt to levels needed to meet the convergence criteria for the European Monetary Union (EMU).
"We've calcuated the effect on the bdget deficit," said a source in the Finance Ministry quoted by Dagens Industri.
Under the Maastricht treaty, state debt should not equal more than 60 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
But the National Institute of Economic Research expected Sweden's debt to increase to 79 percent of GDP this year from 78.7 percent in 1995.
